title: Microscopic QED origin of spin entanglement
abstract: We study effective spin interactions arising from quantum electrodynamics (QED) scattering between localized fermionic spins. By integrating out photon and mediator fields, the dynamics reduce to an effective spin Hamiltonian.   For two qubits in the nonrelativistic regime, the resulting interaction takes a tensor dipolar form with an asymptotic decay proportional to \(R^{-3}\). We obtain analytical expressions for the entanglement negativity, highlighting its dependence on coupling strength and spatial configuration.   We then examine a setup in which two bath spins interact via a sequential exchange with an intermediate fermionic mediator. At the perturbative order considered, the mediator remains unentangled and induces an effective bath--bath interaction with stronger spatial suppression than in the photon-mediated case.   Extending the construction to an \(N\)-spin setting yields an effective interaction network mediated by virtual exchange processes, which can support the generation of multipartite entanglement across the system.
summary: This paper derives the effective spin Hamiltonian governing entanglement generation between localized fermionic qubits by integrating out virtual photon fields from QED. The resulting interactions are dipolar and anisotropic, allowing for the calculation of entanglement measures like negativity over time. It provides a rigorous theoretical framework connecting fundamental field theory to quantum information dynamics.
main_problem: The study aims to derive effective spin Hamiltonians governing entanglement generation from fundamental microscopic Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) scattering processes.
main_result: The derived effective interaction is dipolar, leading to an XXZ-type Hamiltonian for two qubits and complex multi-body interactions for three or more spins. The system can generate bipartite and multipartite entanglement, reaching maximum negativity values.
method: The methodology involves integrating out photon/mediator fields from the full QED Lagrangian to obtain a low-energy effective spin interaction Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{	ext{eff}}$). Time evolution is then analyzed using the von Neumann or Quantum Boltzmann Equation formalism.
model_or_system: The model consists of localized fermionic spins (qubits) interacting via virtual photon exchange. The analysis progresses from two qubits to three-body systems, yielding effective spin-spin coupling terms that decay with distance ($R^{-3}$ or $R^{-4}$).
key_observables: Entanglement negativity ($N(t)$), which quantifies bipartite correlations; the time evolution of the density matrix $ho(t)$.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($\Gamma_{	ext{SS}}(R)$), spatial separation ($R$), and system size ($N$). The nonrelativistic limit is crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the Born-Markov approximation, treating the mediator fields as unentangled, and taking the nonrelativistic limit for propagators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the photon-mediated spin-spin interaction between two qubits and the Feynman diagram structure for three-body QED interactions involving multiple mediators.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives effective Hamiltonians by integrating out field degrees of freedom, first addressing the two-qubit case to find dipolar coupling, then extending the formalism to three or more spins using multi-photon exchange diagrams and master equations.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental microscopic derivation for engineered quantum interactions (like dipole-dipole couplings) that are essential building blocks for quantum computation protocols, linking high-energy physics (QED) directly to quantum information dynamics.
